import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import statsmodels.api as sm
from statsmodels.regression.mixed_linear_model import MixedLM
from scipy.stats import norm, pearsonr

# 1. Load data
df = pd.read_csv('reef.csv')

# 2. Aggregate by reef-year
agg = df.groupby(['id_reef', 'year']).agg(
    total_biomass=('biomass', 'sum'),
    total_prod=('prod', 'sum'),
    mean_sst=('mean_sst', 'mean')
).reset_index()
# Remove zero biomass entries to avoid division
agg = agg[agg['total_biomass'] > 0]
# Compute P/B
agg['P_B'] = agg['total_prod'] / agg['total_biomass']

# 3. Compute long-term medians and means per reef
reef_stats = agg.groupby('id_reef').agg(
    P_B_median=('P_B', 'median'),
    mean_sst_mean=('mean_sst', 'mean')
).reset_index()

# Merge and compute anomalies
df2 = agg.merge(reef_stats, on='id_reef')
df2['P_B_anomaly'] = df2['P_B'] - df2['P_B_median']
df2['SST_anomaly'] = df2['mean_sst'] - df2['mean_sst_mean']

# Drop any inf/nan
df2 = df2.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
df2 = df2.dropna(subset=['P_B_anomaly', 'SST_anomaly'])

# 4. Fit mixed-effects model: P_B_anomaly ~ SST_anomaly + (1|id_reef)
exog = sm.add_constant(df2['SST_anomaly'])
md = MixedLM(endog=df2['P_B_anomaly'], exog=exog, groups=df2['id_reef'])
mdf = md.fit(reml=False)

# Extract fixed-effect results
slope = mdf.params['SST_anomaly']
se = mdf.bse['SST_anomaly']
z = slope / se
p_value = 2 * (1 - norm.cdf(abs(z)))

# 5. Print model summary for SST_anomaly
print("Mixed-effects model: P_B_anomaly ~ SST_anomaly + (1|id_reef)")
print(f"Slope estimate: {slope:.4f}")
print(f"Standard error: {se:.4f}")
print(f"z-value: {z:.2f}")
print(f"p-value: {p_value:.4f}\n")

# 6. Plot anomalies vs anomalies with regression line and 95% CI
x = df2['SST_anomaly']
y = df2['P_B_anomaly']
intercept = mdf.params['const']

y_fit = intercept + slope * x
slope_low, slope_high = slope - 1.96 * se, slope + 1.96 * se
upper = intercept + slope_high * x
lower = intercept + slope_low * x

plt.figure(figsize=(8, 6))
plt.scatter(x, y, alpha=0.4, label='Data')
idx = np.argsort(x)
plt.plot(x.iloc[idx], y_fit.iloc[idx], color='red', label='Fit')
plt.fill_between(x.iloc[idx], lower.iloc[idx], upper.iloc[idx], color='red', alpha=0.2, label='95% CI')
plt.axhline(0, color='gray', linestyle='--', linewidth=0.7)
plt.xlabel('SST anomaly (°C)')
plt.ylabel('P/B anomaly')
plt.title('P/B Anomaly vs SST Anomaly')
plt.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# 7. Correlations per reef
corrs = []
for reef_id, group in df2.groupby('id_reef'):
    if len(group) >= 3 and group['P_B_anomaly'].std() > 0 and group['SST_anomaly'].std() > 0:
        r, _ = pearsonr(group['SST_anomaly'], group['P_B_anomaly'])
    else:
        r = np.nan
    corrs.append({'id_reef': reef_id, 'PB_SST_corr': r})
corr_df = pd.DataFrame(corrs)

# Overall correlation
overall_r, overall_p = pearsonr(df2['SST_anomaly'], df2['P_B_anomaly'])

print("Per-reef Pearson correlations between P/B_anomaly and SST_anomaly:")
print(corr_df.to_string(index=False))
print(f"\nOverall Pearson correlation: r = {overall_r:.3f}, p = {overall_p:.4f}")

{"code":"import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import statsmodels.api as sm
from statsmodels.regression.mixed_linear_model import MixedLM
from scipy.stats import norm, pearsonr

# 1. Load data
df = pd.read_csv('reef.csv')

# 2. Aggregate by reef-year
agg = df.groupby(['id_reef', 'year']).agg(
    total_biomass=('biomass', 'sum'),
    total_prod=('prod', 'sum'),
    mean_sst=('mean_sst', 'mean')
).reset_index()
# Remove zero biomass entries to avoid division
agg = agg[agg['total_biomass'] > 0]
# Compute P/B
agg['P_B'] = agg['total_prod'] / agg['total_biomass']

# 3. Compute long-term medians and means per reef
reef_stats = agg.groupby('id_reef').agg(
    P_B_median=('P_B', 'median'),
    mean_sst_mean=('mean_sst', 'mean')
).reset_index()

# Merge and compute anomalies
df2 = agg.merge(reef_stats, on='id_reef')
df2['P_B_anomaly'] = df2['P_B'] - df2['P_B_median']
df2['SST_anomaly'] = df2['mean_sst'] - df2['mean_sst_mean']

# Drop any inf/nan
df2 = df2.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
df2 = df2.dropna(subset=['P_B_anomaly', 'SST_anomaly'])

# 4. Fit mixed-effects model: P_B_anomaly ~ SST_anomaly + (1|id_reef)
exog = sm.add_constant(df2['SST_anomaly'])
md = MixedLM(endog=df2['P_B_anomaly'], exog=exog, groups=df2['id_reef'])
mdf = md.fit(reml=False)

# Extract fixed-effect results
slope = mdf.params['SST_anomaly']
se = mdf.bse['SST_anomaly']
z = slope / se
p_value = 2 * (1 - norm.cdf(abs(z)))

# 5. Print model summary for SST_anomaly
print("Mixed-effects model: P_B_anomaly ~ SST_anomaly + (1|id_reef)")
print(f"Slope estimate: {slope:.4f}")
print(f"Standard error: {se:.4f}")
print(f"z-value: {z:.2f}")
print(f"p-value: {p_value:.4f}\n")

# 6. Plot anomalies vs anomalies with regression line and 95% CI
x = df2['SST_anomaly']
y = df2['P_B_anomaly']
intercept = mdf.params['const']

y_fit = intercept + slope * x
slope_low, slope_high = slope - 1.96 * se, slope + 1.96 * se
upper = intercept + slope_high * x
lower = intercept + slope_low * x

plt.figure(figsize=(8, 6))
plt.scatter(x, y, alpha=0.4, label='Data')
idx = np.argsort(x)
plt.plot(x.iloc[idx], y_fit.iloc[idx], color='red', label='Fit')
plt.fill_between(x.iloc[idx], lower.iloc[idx], upper.iloc[idx], color='red', alpha=0.2, label='95% CI')
plt.axhline(0, color='gray', linestyle='--', linewidth=0.7)
plt.xlabel('SST anomaly (°C)')
plt.ylabel('P/B anomaly')
plt.title('P/B Anomaly vs SST Anomaly')
plt.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# 7. Correlations per reef
corrs = []
for reef_id, group in df2.groupby('id_reef'):
    if len(group) >= 3 and group['P_B_anomaly'].std() > 0 and group['SST_anomaly'].std() > 0:
        r, _ = pearsonr(group['SST_anomaly'], group['P_B_anomaly'])
    else:
        r = np.nan
    corrs.append({'id_reef': reef_id, 'PB_SST_corr': r})
corr_df = pd.DataFrame(corrs)

# Overall correlation
overall_r, overall_p = pearsonr(df2['SST_anomaly'], df2['P_B_anomaly'])

print("Per-reef Pearson correlations between P/B_anomaly and SST_anomaly:")
print(corr_df.to_string(index=False))
print(f"\nOverall Pearson correlation: r = {overall_r:.3f}, p = {overall_p:.4f}")"}
